io.name: clk
io.description: Clock input; all state updates on the positive edge.

io.name: reset
io.description: Synchronous active-high reset. When high at a positive clock edge, all counter digits and enables are cleared to 0.

io.name: q
io.description: 4-digit BCD counter value. q[3:0]=ones, q[7:4]=tens, q[11:8]=hundreds, q[15:12]=thousands. Each nibble is a valid BCD digit (0-9).

io.name: ena
io.description: Enable signals for upper digits. ena[0] indicates tens digit should increment (ones digit is 9), ena[1] indicates hundreds digit should increment (ones and tens are 9), ena[2] indicates thousands digit should increment (ones, tens, and hundreds are 9).

functional_summary.overview: A 4-digit binary-coded decimal (BCD) counter. On each positive clock edge (when reset is low), the 16-bit output q is incremented as a BCD number, rolling over from 9999 to 0000. The 3-bit ena output indicates which upper digits will increment on the next count, based on the current digit values.
rules: On a positive clock edge with reset=1, q is set to 16'h0000 and ena is set to 3'b000.

On a positive clock edge with reset=0, q is incremented as a 4-digit BCD counter: ones digit increments; if ones was 9 it wraps to 0 and tens increments; cascading through hundreds and thousands; 9999 wraps to 0000.
ena[0] = 1 iff the current ones digit (q[3:0]) equals 9 (tens digit will increment on next count).
ena[1] = 1 iff the current ones and tens digits are both 9 (hundreds digit will increment on next count).
ena[2] = 1 iff the current ones, tens, and hundreds digits are all 9 (thousands digit will increment on next count).
All outputs update synchronously with the positive clock edge; ena reflects the state after the same edge as q (i.e., ena is derived from the current q value).
